construction: after tape file 8's filemark, a foreign file of 2 records is appended, with its trailing filemark

scanner.reasoning: The terminal suffix is intact at its planned positions, but the appended file puts the tape's EOD at 36 + 2N against a planned EOD of 33 + 2N. Spacing back over five filemarks: foreign record (magic miss); C's footer at its recorded position, layout not used because its planned EOD lies before the tape's EOD; BC's separation footer; B's footer, layout not used for the same reason; AB's separation footer. A's footer is never reached, and its layout would not be used either. No footer supplies a layout, so no replica validates, even though all three replicas are intact.
scanner.then: Returns BotStructuralRecoveryRequired, performs the Section 8.4.1 walk, and reports that terminal authority was not recovered.
quotes: locate, from EOD, the local footer of a terminal replica, and from it the planned terminal layout (Section 8.3); the Scanner spaces back over up to five filemarks from EOD and reads the record before each, stopping early when a backspace does not cross exactly one filemark or leaves the partition.

A terminal replica's footer that parses supplies a planned layout only when its recorded footer position equals the position at which it was read, and the layout's planned EOD is at or after the tape's EOD.
A layout whose planned EOD lies before the tape's EOD may be followed by later tape files, so it is not used, and when no footer supplies a layout, no replica validates;
if no replica validates, perform the BOT structural recovery walk in Section 8.4.1.

If A, B, and C all fail, the Scanner returns an explicit `BotStructuralRecoveryRequired` outcome and performs the Section 8.4.1 walk; BOT Object classifications are likewise streamed before their terminal summary.
A normal finalized tape has the exact terminal suffix of Section 8.3 and EOD immediately after C's trailing filemark.
The walk does not invent a terminal replica. The Scanner MUST report that terminal authority was not recovered.

tape_files.1: Object candidate by elimination (item 7); identity unknown
tape_files.9: foreign file of 2 records after the exact terminal suffix: preferred reading, nonconformant and not admitted as an Object (Section 12.6); OPEN, see open_points

walk.ends: EOD at the start of tape file 10
open_points: Tape file 9. The exact terminal suffix is present, so Section 12.6's rule reaches this file if a foreign file is a 'structural artifact', a term the text does not define. Permitted: (a) nonconformant trailing file, not admitted as an Object (preferred: the rule has force only for files the ladder would otherwise put in item 7); (b) Object candidate by elimination (item 7), identity unknown, outside the validated scope. Validation of files 0..3 is unaffected.
quotes: A structural artifact after the exact terminal suffix is nonconformant and MUST NOT be admitted as an Object.
Item 7 applies to a tape file that none of items 1 to 6 recognises.

A map produced by the Section 8.4.1 walk, after the second pass of Section 12.3, is validated against the tape's final ParityMap when that ParityMap validates and is marked `is_final_directory`, and the map's canonical projection (Section 7.3) through the ParityMap's own entry hashes to its `canonical_map_digest`.
The validated scope and durable boundary are the first `directory_scope_tape_file_count` tape files, ending with that ParityMap's entry; `W` is `directory_scope_highest_protected_ordinal`.
MUST treat rows beyond the validated prefix as forensic only, never as recovery inputs.
